goldens.comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

goldens.comment: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

candidates: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131 - A backup code alone signs in without the password if any totpCode is also sent.. The password check above only runs when `!credentials.totpCode`. A client can send `email`, an empty `password`, any non-empty `totpCode` and a valid `backupCode`. The password check is skipped, and then this branch is taken because `credentials.backupCode` is set, so the TOTP is never checked either. The backup code becomes the only factor. It is a static 40-bit value, and there are ten of them per user. The fix is to verify the password inside the backup-code branch whenever `user.password` is set, or to make the password skip depend on a valid TOTP rather than on whether `totpCode` is present.

apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:266 - Dismissing the backup-codes dialog skips resetState and onEnable. 2FA is already enabled on the server when the backup-codes step appears. `resetState()` and `onEnable()` only run from the Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog with Escape, the X, or an outside click, `onOpenChange` runs instead. The parent is never told 2FA was enabled, so its switch stays stale. `step` also stays at `DisplayBackupCodes`, so reopening the modal shows the old codes instead of the password step. Route dialog dismissal on this step through the same handler, for example by wrapping `onOpenChange` so it calls `resetState()` and `onEnable()` when `step === SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes`.

packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:147 - Backup code consumption is a read-modify-write with no concurrency guard, so one code can be used more than once.. The code reads `backupCodes`, checks the submitted code, then writes the list back unconditionally. If two login requests with the same code arrive at the same time, both read the list before either writes, both pass the check, and both log in. One-time use is lost. The fix is to make the update conditional on the stored value being unchanged (for example `updateMany` with `where: { id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes }`, failing if the count is 0) or to run it in a serializable transaction.
